app.title: Voice workshop
app.subtitle: Make up the people you hear on the radio
login.heading: Log in
login.intro: Ask the adult who runs the radio for the password.
login.locked: Too many failed attempts: try again in {seconds} s.
welcome.title: Welcome to the voice workshop
welcome.text: Here you make up the people who answer on the radio: who they are, when they listen, what they know and what they ask of you.
welcome.step1: Pick a voice on the left, or click "+ New voice".
welcome.step2: Answer the questions, step by step, then click Save.
welcome.step3: The game hears your voice by itself, no restart.
voices.title: Your voices
status.delivered.help: A voice that comes with the game, as it is
status.removed.help: An original voice you took off the air
status.outdated.help: The game will replace it with the new version next time the world loads.
new.title: New voice
editor.removed_help: This voice is off the air. Go back to the original to hear it again.
editor.all_steps_help: Also shows the steps this voice does not use yet.
confirm.remove: Take "{name}" off the air? You can bring it back.
confirm.restore: Put "{name}" back as it was? Your changes will be lost.
confirm.leave: Your changes are not saved. Leave this voice anyway?
checks.title: To check: {n}
checks.judge: These are tips: you can save anyway, the game decides.
checks.saved_anyway: ({n} tip(s) left: the game will say if something is wrong.)
who.name: What is this voice called?
who.description: In one sentence, who is it?
who.description_placeholder: E.g. A nurse who wants to go back to her clinic
who.description_help: For you only: the game does not read it.
where.radio: Which radio does the player need to hear it?
where.radio_help: The game gives her a frequency only this radio picks up.
where.radio_fixed: The badge tells which radio picks up your frequency.
where.fixed_help: The same in every game, in steps of 0.2.
where.badge_none: No radio tunes this frequency: from {min} to {max} MHz, in steps of {step}.
radio.any_talkie.name: Any walkie-talkie
radio.any_talkie.who: Everybody hears it, even with a toy or homemade walkie.
radio.good_talkie.name: A good walkie-talkie
radio.good_talkie.who: Needs at least a ValuTech walkie-talkie.
radio.pro_talkie.name: A pro walkie-talkie
radio.pro_talkie.who: Needs at least a Premium Technologies walkie-talkie.
radio.tactical.name: A tactical walkie or a ham radio
radio.tactical.who: Needs a tactical walkie, a ham radio or better.
radio.military.name: Military gear
radio.military.who: Only the army walkie, the manpack radio and the army ham radio hear it.
choice.location.rescue: The game places her for a rescue
where.coords_help: Record the square in game (right click), or read it on the map.
where.call: What she says when she calls
where.call_help: The button puts her frequency in the sentence.
where.call_placeholder: E.g. Anyone out there? This is Mae on [frequency]. Over.
personality.actions_help: She always talks. Tick what else she does.
recipehelp.title: Recipe help
recipehelp.jobs_help: She helps the player find a recipe of these trades. None ticked: she does not help.
recipehelp.jobs.makeshift.help: Everything else, recipes of other mods included.
recipehelp.from_help: Below that, she says no in her own way.
recipehelp.delay_help: If she searches, the player calls her back later.
recipehelp.delay.half_day: She searches for half a day
help.help.jobs.what: The trades the voice knows about. The player asks her how to make something; she looks among the recipes of these trades, mods included.
help.help.jobs.example: A nurse: Medical. A farmer: Farming and Cooking.
help.help.jobs.game: The player asks on the radio, in their own language, how to make an item. She answers in her own words.
help.help.jobs.tip: Pick what her job and her past explain. Makeshift: everything that is in no other trade.
help.help.jobs.cooking.what: Meals, preserves, bread: anything you make to eat.
help.help.jobs.electrical.what: Wires, batteries, radios, small gadgets to tinker with.
help.help.jobs.farming.what: Seeds, fertiliser, garden tools and crop care.
help.help.jobs.makeshift.what: Everything else: survival tricks, fishing, repairs, mod recipes with no trade.
help.help.from.what: The reputation needed with her before she helps.
help.help.from.neutral.what: She helps, except those who wronged her.
help.help.from.good.what: She only helps those who already helped her.
help.help.delay.what: Whether she answers during the call or searches first. Durations are game hours.
help.help.delay.tip: A voice who has to dig through her books searches for a long time; a voice who knows answers during the call.
help.help.delay.now.what: She gives the recipe during the call.
help.help.delay.hour.what: She says to call back in an hour.
help.help.delay.half_day.what: She says to call back in twelve hours.
help.help.delay.day.what: She says to call back the next day.
personality.shares: She can give the contact of…
personality.shares_help: A trusted player gets the frequency of one of these voices.
personality.prompt_help: Her past, what she knows, her secrets, how she talks. The AI plays the voice from this text.
personality.language: Which language do you write her personality in?
personality.language_help: The AI reads both: write in the language you like.
ai.unavailable: The AI is not plugged in: ask the adult who runs the workshop.
ai.describe: Describe the character in a few sentences
ai.describe_placeholder: A tired nurse who left the clinic and wants to go back...
ai.describe_help: Write 2 or 3 sentences, the AI does the rest (in English).
ai.replace_confirm: Replace the current personality with this text?
ai.propose_help: The AI gives you an idea for this box, from everything you already wrote. Click again for another idea.
ai.try_help: Talk to her like a player, even before saving. Nothing changes in the game.
ai.try_empty: Say something to start the conversation.
action.mark_map.help: Puts one of her places on your map.
action.reveal_area.help: Uncovers a neighbourhood on your map.
action.place_scene.help: Places a scene in the world.
action.start_mission.help: The missions of the step "Places and missions".
action.persona_state.help: Her mood and supplies change from call to call.
action.propose_trade.help: Fill in the trade of the step "Rewards".
action.report_mission.help: Players report a job on the radio.
action.share_frequency.help: Gives the frequency of another voice.
missions.question: Her missions
missions.none: No mission yet: pick one below.
mission.story_placeholder: E.g. I need to know what is left of my clinic.
mission.story_help: One sentence, in the language of her personality.
mission.target_help: Near, further or far from the player: a building picked for each mission. Or a place.
mission.drops_help: The player drops off at any of the ticked ones.
mission.after_help: The job is offered once this other mission succeeded.
mission.weight_help: When the voice has several missions to give: the ones it offers most often.
mission.scope_help: For "Only after": the player alone, or the whole team.
mission.sets_state_help: When the mission succeeds. The AI will remember it.
mission.scout.help: Visit a building and report what you saw.
mission.clear.help: Kill the zombies around a place.
mission.barricade.help: Board up the outside windows and doors of a building.
mission.deliver.help: Leave the requested goods at a dead drop.
mission.retrieve.help: Find the ID card of a missing person and leave it at a dead drop.
mission.item.help: Find one precious object at a place and leave it at a dead drop.
mission.relay.help: Put a working two-way radio, turned on, upstairs or on the roof of a place.
mission.route.help: Go through several places in order, on foot or by car, then report.
mission.signal.help: Light a Signal Smoke signal at a place.
mission.watch.help: Stay near a place for some game hours, then say what you saw.
mission.sets_state_placeholder: E.g. She went back to her clinic
mission.building_help: The game picks one of this kind for each mission.
param.quantity.help: The game draws a number between the two.
param.collect_hours.help: The time with nobody near the dead drop.
param.item.help: An item of the game, picked in the list.
param.label: What she calls it
param.label.help: What the voice calls the object.
param.points.help: 2 to 8 exact spots, picked from the places.
browser.title: Pick an item of the game
browser.more: First {shown} of {n}: narrow the search or pick a category.
browser.none: No item matches. Try another word or "All categories".
lot.name: Name of the bundle
lot.empty: This bundle is empty: add items.
trade.q_pay: What does she take as payment?
trade.add_taken: Add what she takes as payment
note.text_intro: What the player reads. The button puts in her frequency.
note.too_long: Too long: make the sentence shorter.
note.needs_frequency: Put your frequency in a line (button "Add my frequency").
note.own_item: This note is set by the mod.
lootbrowser.title: Pick a piece of furniture
lootbrowser.results: Furniture and containers of the game
lootbrowser.more: The first {shown} of {n}: narrow your search or pick a kind.
lootbrowser.none: Nothing matches. Try another word or "All kinds".
help.ui.lootbrowser_browser.what: The game's furniture and containers: search by word, filter by kind, tick, then "Add selected". Their names are never typed.
help.ui.lootbrowser_browser.example: Kind "Shops and restaurants", search "fishing": Fishing store gear.
help.ui.lootbrowser_browser.tip: The note is already wherever papers are found: only add places that suit your voice.
help.ui.lootbrowser_category.what: Shows one kind of place only: home, offices, shops, crates, vehicles.
section.advanced_help: Used by the voices of the mod. A new voice does not need them.
places.title: Places of every voice
places.help: A place is shared by every voice: an exact spot or an area. Each voice picks its own from a list.
places.label: Name on the map
places.label_help: Players see it. Every voice uses it.
places.at_help: Record the square in game, or read it on the map. Floor 0 is the ground floor.
map.title: Build 42 map (zomboidmap.com), in a new tab
map.paste_tip: Tip: on the map, copy the position, then paste it here.
places.empty: No place yet. Start with a spot you know.
places.kind.point.help: One square: a door, a dumpster, a pier.
places.kind.zone.help: A rectangle: the game picks a building in it for each mission.
places.points_only: An exact spot is needed here: the player must find the very square.
places.corner_help: Paste two positions from the map, across the diagonal.
places.check.no_square: Say where it is on the map.
places.check.zone_too_big: This area is too big: 1,500 squares a side at most.
places.new_help: It joins the places of every voice, then you come back here.
places.saved: Places saved. The game reads them within 30 seconds.
places.unfinished: Not saved yet: finish the place "{name}".
places.in_use: "{name}" is used by {voices}: take it out of these voices first.
places.pick: Pick a place in the list to change it, or make a new one.
surveys.title: From my records
surveys.help: While playing, right click a square to note it.
surveys.none: No record yet. In game: right click a square, "Voice workshop: record this place".
surveys.unreadable: The records cannot be read: is the workshop running?
surveys.ask: Name of the place on the map (you can change it later):
rewards.question: What does a player win after a job?
rewards.help: Only one reward is drawn at random.
rewards.none: No reward: after a job the voice marks one of its places on the map.
rewards.cache_place: Where does she hide the supply bag?
rewards.cache_place_help: An exact spot, marked on the map of the player.
reward.cache.help: A bag of goods from a category, left at the voice's first dead drop.
reward.frequency.help: The frequency of a voice she can pass on.
reward.stashmap.help: A map of a hidden stash.
advanced.title: To go further
advanced.trade.help: She swaps items in secret with the players.
advanced.note.help: A note gives her frequency. It is already hidden wherever papers are found, in glove boxes and on zombies.
advanced.note.enable: The frequency is on a note
advanced.category.help: Item lists of her own, for her deliveries and bags.
advanced.action_added: "{action}" is ticked too in the step Personality.
key.trade.landing.help: Tick the places where the merchant meets the players.
accept.no_value: Traders buy nothing from this list: untick it.
key.note.text.help: 40 signs per line (an accented letter counts double), 8 lines at most.
import.drop: Drop the file of a voice here
import.exists: A voice already has this name ({name}).

check.radio_and_frequency: Choose either a radio or a fixed frequency, not both.
check.bad_frequency: No radio tunes this frequency: {value} (a number with one decimal, from 0.2 to 1000.0, in steps of 0.2).
check.bad_hours: Custom hours: each range needs a different start and end.
check.bad_section_id: A part of the voice has a name that does not work: "{value}".
check.duplicate_section: Two parts have the same name "{value}".
check.bad_range: {name}: a number, or two numbers, the smaller first.
check.unknown_place: {name}: pick a place from the list.

check.not_sellable: {value}: traders do not sell this item. Remove this line.
check.no_accept: The trade must say what she takes as payment: tick a list or add an item.
check.accept_not_sellable: {value}: traders do not buy this item. Remove it from what she takes.
check.accept_no_value: List {value}: traders buy nothing from it. Untick it.
check.accept_unknown_category: What she takes names a list that does not exist: {value}.
check.needs_drop: This mission needs a dead drop: tick a place.
check.unknown_mission: "Only after" names a mission that no longer exists.
check.bad_weight: {name}: the chances must be 1 or more.
check.place_is_zone: {name}: an exact spot is needed here, not an area.
check.building_needs_zone: A kind of building goes with an area or a distance, not an exact spot.
check.needs_cache_place: Say where she hides the supply bag.

code.sheet_refused: The voice is not complete yet: fix the points shown before chatting with her.
code.places_saved: Places saved. The game reads them within 30 seconds.
code.places_unfinished: First finish the place "{name}" in the Places tab.
dashboard.title: Voices dashboard
dashboard.help: All your voices at a glance. Click a voice to open it.
dashboard.none: No voice yet. Make your first one with "+ New voice".
dashboard.col.name: Voice
dashboard.tile.gap: a day when only the "day and night" voices listen
verdict.dot: The game could not read this voice
verdict.title: The voice does not work yet: fix it in the step "{step}"
verdict.title_noline: The voice does not work yet
verdict.silent: The game keeps the older version meanwhile.
verdict.changed: You changed this voice: the game has not read it again yet. Its answer will show here.
verdict.why.unknown_key: The setting "{name}" does not exist here: check its name or remove it.
verdict.why.duplicate_key: The setting "{name}" is written twice: keep a single line.
verdict.why.missing_key: The setting "{name}" is missing: fill it in.
verdict.why.empty_value: The setting "{name}" is empty: give it a value or remove it.
verdict.why.frequency: A frequency is wrong: a number with one decimal (145.0), from 0.2 to 1000.0 MHz, on the 0.2 step of the radios.
verdict.why.radio: Give either the radio needed (radio) or one fixed frequency (frequency): only one of them.
verdict.why.hours: The listening hours do not work: pick them with the cards of "When does she listen?".
verdict.why.unknown_section: A part of this voice is unknown to the game.
verdict.why.unknown_ref: "{name}" exists nowhere in the voice (place, mission or list).
verdict.why.mission_type: The mission type "{name}" does not exist.
verdict.why.prompt: The personality is missing or empty: write it in the "Personality" step.
verdict.why.encoding: The file is not saved as plain UTF-8: save it from the workshop.
verdict.why.other: The game does not understand part of this voice.
journal.title: Live journal
journal.help: The lines of the bridge (what players say to the voices, replies, errors) and the sheet lines written by the game, live. Read-only, on this machine only: they hold the players’ dialogues.
journal.no_bridge: The bridge is not running (the AI is not configured): only the game lines show here, and the voices do not answer in game.
journal.no_game_log: Game console not found: start the workshop again with --game-log <file> to see the game lines.
journal.game_log_missing: The game console does not exist yet ({path}): its lines will show once the game runs.
help.head.id.what: The voice's inner name: the workshop makes it from her first name, you never deal with it.
help.head.name.what: The name of the character, the way they introduce themselves.
help.head.name.game: Players hear it on the radio.
help.head.format.what: The version of the voice's text.
help.head.format.tip: You do not need to touch it: the workshop fills it in for you.
help.head.language.what: The language you write her personality in: English or French.
help.head.language.game: The AI reads both. The voice answers in the player's language.
help.head.language.tip: Nothing is translated: your text stays as you wrote it.
help.head.radio.what: The radio the player needs to hear this voice and talk to it.
help.head.radio.game: The game gives the voice a free frequency that this radio tunes and simpler radios do not: the player needs the right radio, then looks for the voice by turning the dial. The frequency changes with every new game.
help.head.radio.tip: For a first voice, keep “Any walkie-talkie”: everybody hears it.
help.head.radio.any_talkie.what: Every walkie-talkie and ham radio, even the toy or homemade walkie (75 to 150 MHz).
help.head.radio.good_talkie.what: A ValuTech walkie-talkie or better (50 to 200 MHz).
help.head.radio.pro_talkie.what: A Premium Technologies walkie-talkie or better (25 to 300 MHz).
help.head.radio.tactical.what: A tactical walkie, a ham radio or better (10 to 500 MHz).
help.head.radio.military.what: The army walkie, the manpack radio or the army ham radio (0.2 to 1000 MHz).
help.head.frequency.what: One fixed frequency, the same in every game, instead of the draw.
help.head.frequency.game: Players can write it down once and for all and pass it around.
help.head.frequency.tip: The badge tells which radio tunes it. Avoid the frequency of another voice.
help.head.listen.what: The hours when she listens to the radio.
help.head.listen.game: Outside those hours the voice stays silent and makes no call.
help.head.listen.example: At night: from 8 pm to 6 am.
help.head.listen.tip: With custom hours, a range can go past midnight (10 pm to 6 am).
help.head.location.what: Where the voice is on the map.
help.head.location.tip: For a new voice, "nowhere" is fine.
help.head.location.none.what: It is nowhere on the map.
help.head.location.fixed.what: It is at a precise point of the map, which you give with x, y, z.
help.head.location.rescue.what: The game chooses the place, for a rescue.
help.head.location.rescue.tip: This choice is kept for the rescue of the Whitakers.
help.head.coords.what: The tile where the voice is: x, y, then the floor z (0 = ground floor).
help.head.coords.tip: Safest: record it in game (right click on the square). "See on the map" shows the square.
help.head.state.what: The state of the voice in the story.
help.head.state.active.what: The voice listens and answers. This is the normal choice.
help.head.state.silent.what: The voice keeps its frequency but does not answer, as if paused.
help.head.state.gone.what: The voice left the radio. Its frequency is free again.
help.head.state.gone.tip: It can come back later if you change this state.
help.head.state.dead.what: The voice is dead in the story. Its frequency is free again.
help.head.shares.what: The other voices whose frequency this one may give away.
help.head.shares.game: The game itself picks an active voice among them and adds it to the notebook of the player.
help.head.shares.tip: Used by "Give a contact" and the reward "A radio contact".
help.head.budget.what: How many requests the voice accepts per real hour. 0: only the general limit of the mod counts.
help.head.budget.game: Beyond that, the voice stays silent until the next hour.
help.head.budget.tip: It keeps the cost of the AI down.
help.head.call_one_in.what: Whether the voice calls by herself, and how often.
help.head.call_one_in.game: The player hears it call without having asked anything, during its listening hours.
help.head.call_one_in.example: Often: about one call every 3 game hours.
help.head.call_one_in.tip: "Exact value": one chance in this number, each game hour.
help.head.call_text.what: The call text of an original voice, kept in the mod's translations.
help.head.call_text.tip: A new voice writes what she says instead.
help.head.call.what: What the voice says when she calls by herself. The button puts in her frequency.
help.head.call.game: Every player listening on its frequency hears this call on the radio.
help.head.call.example: Anyone out there? This is Mae on [frequency]. Over.
help.head.actions.what: What the voice can do in the game, besides talking.
help.head.actions.game: During the conversation, the AI decides by itself to use an action when it fits. The game then checks every action; if it is refused, the voice still talks.
help.head.actions.tip: Tick only what the voice needs.
help.head.actions.say.what: The voice answers on the radio.
help.head.actions.persona_state.what: The morale and the supplies of the voice change over the calls.
help.head.actions.persona_state.game: It then talks about it by itself, for instance if it moved.
help.head.actions.persona_state.tip: It is only story: nothing changes in the game.
help.head.actions.mark_map.what: The voice puts a marker on the map of the player.
help.head.actions.mark_map.game: It says "I am marking it on your map" and a symbol appears, at one of its places.
help.head.actions.mark_map.tip: Needs a place ticked under "Which places can she mark on the map?". Only the player who talks sees it.
help.head.actions.reveal_area.what: The voice reveals a neighbourhood on the map of the player.
help.head.actions.reveal_area.game: It describes a place it knows, and the area appears on the map.
help.head.actions.reveal_area.tip: Needs a place ticked under "Which places can she mark on the map?". Only the player who talks sees it.
help.head.actions.signal.tip: For now, the game always refuses this action.
help.head.actions.place_cache.tip: This action is kept for the notebook recovery missions: do not set it in a sheet.
help.head.actions.place_scene.tip: For now, the game always refuses this action.
help.head.actions.start_mission.what: The voice gives missions to the player.
help.head.actions.start_mission.game: The player must have the notebook. After a successful mission, they get reputation and a reward.
help.head.actions.start_mission.tip: Pick the missions in the step "Places and missions".
help.head.actions.propose_trade.what: The voice sells goods to players.
help.head.actions.propose_trade.game: It sets a meeting for a no-contact exchange.
help.head.actions.propose_trade.tip: Fill in the trade of the step "Rewards" too.
help.head.actions.report_mission.what: Players can report on a mission over the radio.
help.head.actions.share_frequency.what: The voice gives the frequency of another voice to someone it trusts.
help.head.actions.share_frequency.game: The frequency goes into the notebook of the player.
help.head.actions.share_frequency.tip: Then tick the voices she can pass on.
help.head.marks.what: The places the voice may mark on the map of the player.
help.head.marks.game: Used by "Mark a place on the map" and "Show a neighbourhood". An area is marked in its middle.
help.head.marks.tip: With no reward set, the voice also gives one of these markers after a mission. 12 at most.
help.ui.surveys.what: The squares you noted while playing: right click a square, "Voice workshop: record this place".
help.ui.surveys.game: "Add to the places" makes a place on that square, with a name suggested.
help.ui.surveys.example: A dumpster behind the church, recorded in game, becomes the place "Bin - Church".
help.ui.surveys.tip: In solo, the menu needs the game's debug mode; in multiplayer, an admin.
help.place.label.what: The name of the place, as players see it on their map.
help.place.label.tip: No secret here. 48 signs at most.
help.place.at.what: The tile of the place: x, y, then the floor z (0 = ground floor).
help.place.at.game: The AI never sees these numbers.
help.place.at.tip: Most reliable is the in-game record (right click, "Voice workshop: record this place"). "View on the map" shows the square to check it.
help.place.kind.what: An exact spot (one square) or an area (a rectangle).
help.place.kind.game: In an area, the game picks a building people lived in for each mission.
help.place.kind.tip: Dead drops, meeting points, routes and hiding places need an exact spot.
help.place.area.what: Two opposite corners of the area, pasted from the map, and its floor.
help.place.area.tip: 1,500 squares a side at most. A marker of an area goes in its middle.
help.map.what: Opens the Build 42 map of zomboidmap.com in a new tab, centred on the square x, y (on floor z). Without x and y it opens the whole map: the square under the mouse shows its coordinates there.
help.map.example: 10600, 9300, 0 opens the map zoomed on that square.
help.map.tip: The site is not made by the game: its map (Build 42.20) may differ slightly from your version (changed building, new district). For a sure square, record it in the game.
help.mission.type.what: The kind of mission the voice gives.
help.mission.type.tip: The game itself checks that the mission is done: the voice decides nothing.
help.mission.story.what: The reason the voice gives for its request.
help.mission.story.game: The AI receives it with the mission and tells it to the player.
help.mission.story.example: I need to know what is left of my clinic.
help.mission.story.tip: 200 signs at most, in the language of her personality.
help.mission.target.game: Near the player (100 to 200 squares), further away (200 to 500), far away (500 to 1,500): a building picked for each mission. An area: a building picked in it. An exact spot: always the same.
help.mission.target.tip: With no choice, it is near the player.
help.mission.drops.what: The dead drops where the player may leave the things.
help.mission.drops.game: All of them are circled on the map, and the player leaves them wherever they like.
help.mission.drops.tip: Deliver, bring back and find an item need at least one.
help.mission.weight.what: Whether the voice offers this mission rarely, normally or often among several.
help.mission.weight.tip: Normally by default. Often comes up twice as much as Normally.
help.mission.after.what: This mission is only offered once another mission is done.
help.mission.after.game: The player discovers the missions one after the other.
help.mission.scope.what: For "Only after": who must have completed the first mission.
help.mission.scope.character.what: The player themselves must have completed the first mission.
help.mission.scope.team.what: The whole team of the player counts (their faction, or just them if they have none).
help.mission.sets_state.what: What changes for the voice when the mission succeeds, in one sentence.
help.mission.sets_state.game: The AI remembers it at every call.
help.mission.sets_state.example: She went back to her clinic
help.mission.sets_state.tip: Two missions with the same sentence tell the same thing.
help.mission.building.what: The kind of building picked for the mission.
help.mission.building.game: Only for an area or a distance. "Any": the game chooses.
help.mission_type.scout.game: The player visits a building, then reports what they saw.
help.mission_type.clear.game: The player kills the zombies around a place.
help.mission_type.signal.game: The player lights a Signal Smoke signal at the requested place.
help.mission_type.barricade.game: The player boards up outside windows and doors with planks or metal sheets.
help.mission_type.barricade.tip: A place is needed. Only barricades built during the mission count.
help.mission_type.deliver.game: The player leaves the requested items at a dead drop. Drops at several places add up.
help.mission_type.deliver.tip: At least one dead drop is needed.
help.mission_type.retrieve.game: The player finds the ID card of a missing person and leaves it at a dead drop.
help.mission_type.retrieve.tip: At least one dead drop is needed.
help.mission_type.item.game: The game puts a precious item at the chosen place. The player finds it and leaves it at a dead drop.
help.mission_type.item.tip: A place and a dead drop are needed.
help.mission_type.relay.game: The player puts a powered, switched-on radio that can transmit high up (an upper floor or the roof).
help.mission_type.relay.tip: A place is needed. Switched off, without power or removed, the radio no longer counts.
help.mission_type.route.game: The player goes through several places in order, on foot or by vehicle, then reports.
help.mission_type.route.tip: Only the next stop is circled on the map.
help.mission_type.watch.game: The player stays near a place for a few game hours, then tells what they saw.
help.mission_type.watch.tip: A place is needed. Time counts in game hours: it stops when the game is paused.
help.mission_type.barricade.count.what: How many outside windows and doors to barricade.
help.param.collect_hours.what: The game hours before the voice picks up the things at the dead drop.
help.param.collect_hours.game: The pick-up happens out of the sight of the player.
help.param.items.what: The category of the requested items. Only items of this category count.
help.param.items.tip: With no category, the voice asks for 6 bandages or torn sheets.
help.param.quantity.what: How many items are asked: one number, or two numbers for a range.
help.param.quantity.game: The game draws the number at the start of the mission, then it no longer changes.
help.param.item.what: The item to find, picked in the list of the game's items.
help.param.label.what: How the voice calls the item.
help.param.label.game: The player hears it in the request.
help.param.points.what: The places to go through, in order: from 2 to 8 exact spots.
help.param.points.game: The player passes a point by going within 8 tiles of its centre.
help.param.points.tip: Never the same place twice in a row.
help.param.hours.what: The number of game hours to stay at the watch post.
help.param.hours.game: The player must stay within 6 tiles of the place.
help.param_kind.category.what: A category of items, chosen from the list.
help.param_kind.item.what: An item of the game: click "Pick an item", search its name and pick it in the list.
help.param_kind.place.what: An exact spot of the places, picked from the list.
help.param_kind.places.what: Several exact spots of the places, in order.
help.param_kind.range.what: One number, or two numbers for a range: the game draws one.
help.param_kind.skill.what: A game skill, chosen from the list.
help.rewards.pool.what: The list of possible rewards after a successful mission.
help.rewards.pool.game: After each successful mission, the game draws just one at random, following their chances. The player also gains reputation.
help.rewards.pool.example: Bag of supplies: Often; a frequency: Rarely
help.rewards.pool.tip: A reward that is impossible at that moment is not drawn. With no list, the voice gives the marker of one of its places.
help.rewards.cache_place.what: The spot where the voice leaves the supply bag won.
help.rewards.cache_place.game: It is marked on the map of the player.
help.ui.reward_weight.what: Whether this reward comes out rarely, normally or often against the others. Often comes out twice as much as Normally, which comes out twice as much as Rarely. Next to its name, the page says roughly how often it comes out.
help.ui.reward_weight.example: A medical bag on Often and a lesson on Normally: the bag comes out about 2 times in 3.
help.reward.cache.what: A bag of items of one category.
help.reward.cache.game: The bag is put at the first dead drop of the voice. The items are real, in randomly drawn amounts.
help.reward.cache.tip: Say where she hides the supply bag. The player gets that marker, seen only by them.
help.reward.frequency.game: It is written in the notebook of the player.
help.reward.frequency.tip: The possible voices are ticked in the step Personality ("She can give the contact of…").
help.reward.stashmap.what: A map that leads to a hidden stash of the game, not yet searched.
help.reward.stashmap.tip: Only one per player and per voice.
help.reward.lesson.game: The game gives 25 experience points as a base, with a cap of 100 per day.
help.reward.lesson.tip: A character with no bonus in this skill only gets a quarter of it.
help.shared_category.ammo.what: Ammunition: 9 mm bullets and shotgun shells.
help.shared_category.food.what: Tinned food: beans, soup and corn.
help.shared_category.medical.what: Medical supplies: bandages, disinfectant and pills.
help.shared_category.radio.what: Radio gear: a walkie-talkie and batteries.
help.shared_category.tools.what: Tools: a hammer, a screwdriver and nails.
help.shared_category.cash.what: Cash and valuables: money, bundles, gold and silver coins and bars, diamonds.
help.shared_category.jewelry.what: Jewelry: rings, necklaces, bracelets, earrings, watches.
help.shared_category.pictures.what: Cameras and films: cameras and home video tapes.
Papers of the dead: ID cards, passports, wallets, dog tags, badges.
help.shared_category.military_gear.what: Military gear: assault rifle and ammunition, bulletproof vest, gas mask, army pack and boots.
help.ui.own_categories.what: Your own item lists, for deliveries and supply bags.
help.ui.own_categories.game: A category fills a bag, or sets what the player is asked to deliver.
help.ui.item_browser.what: The list of the game's items: search by name, filter by category. You never type an item's name: you pick it here.
help.ui.item_browser.game: Each line gives the item's name and category, as in the inventory.
help.ui.item_browser.tip: "Add items": tick several items (click or Enter), even across searches, then "Add selected". A click on an item already in the list replaces it. Escape closes without any change.
help.ui.item_category.what: Shows only the items of one category, the one the game shows in the inventory.
help.ui.item_category.tip: With a category and no search, the whole category is listed in alphabetical order.
help.category.item.what: The items of the list, added from the list of the game's items, each with its amount.
help.category.item.game: The game draws an amount within the range.
help.ui.description.what: A few words to remind you who this voice is.
help.ui.description.tip: For you only: the game does not read it.
help.ui.prompt.what: The only description of the character: past, skills, what it hides, tone and radio rules. The AI reads this text to play the voice.
help.ui.prompt.example: You are Mae Tolliver, 67, a retired schoolteacher...
help.ui.prompt.game: What the voice learns about the world (deaths, places, missions, news) comes from the game while it is played.
help.ui.prompt.tip: Talk to her in the second person ("You are…"). No server secret: the AI may repeat everything.
help.ui.places.what: The places every voice shares: an exact spot or an area.
help.ui.places.game: A voice only sees the places it picks. The AI reads their names, never the numbers.
help.ui.places.tip: A place a voice uses cannot be deleted: take it out of the voice first.
help.trade.section.what: Trade: the voice barters on the radio and delivers in secret, never showing itself. A deal is two lists of items: what the player brings, what the voice leaves.
help.trade.section.game: No trader ever appears in game, and the player never sees a price. The first deal on the radio books a passage for their group: the place is marked on the map and the deal is written in the notebook. The player leaves exactly what was agreed within 3 squares of the place (never in a vehicle), then goes out of sight; back there, the goods are waiting.
help.trade.section.example: "You bring me 2 boxes of shells, I leave you a bottle of whiskey": at 2 am, lamp lit at the dock, the player hears the boat land, drops the bag and walks away; an hour later the whiskey is in the bag.
help.trade.section.tip: Only what is left after the deal counts. If something is missing, the trader keeps everything and leaves nothing; if nothing is left, the reputation drops a little. A passage is rarely called off (patrol, helicopter, storm): the voice announces it every hour until the meeting.
help.trade.landing.what: The meeting place with the merchant.
help.trade.landing.game: The place is marked on the map of the group that booked, and only theirs. The player puts a bag with the payment there, within 3 squares of the place.
help.trade.arrival.game: Boat or road: during the window, the player shows the signal on the spot, then hears the trader arrive. Dead drop: no signal, the payment waits in the container of the place.
help.trade.arrival.boat.what: A boat lands at the meeting place.
help.trade.arrival.boat.game: During the window, the player shows a lit lamp in hand or a red flare (Signal Smoke) on the spot; they hear the boat's engine as it lands.
help.trade.arrival.road.what: A van parks by the road.
help.trade.arrival.road.game: Same signals as for the boat; you hear the door of the van parked by the roadside.
help.trade.arrival.cache.game: No signal: the player leaves the payment in the container of the place (bin, mailbox) before the hour, and the goods are put there out of sight.
help.trade.arrival.cache.tip: Like the traders of Rosewood, Ekron or Fallas Lake. No noise.
help.trade.every_days.game: The trader only comes back after this many days; each passage is booked by a firm offer on the radio.
help.trade.every_days.tip: "Exact value": a number of days from 1 to 28.
help.trade.hours.what: The time window of the meeting, in game time.
help.trade.hours.game: On the booked night, the player must be at the meeting during this window to show the signal (not for a dead drop).
help.trade.hours.tip: The end may be after midnight: from 23:00 to 01:00.
help.trade.delay_hours.what: How long nobody must hang around the place before the swap.
help.trade.delay_hours.game: The trader only comes if nobody has been within 100 squares (in x and in y) for that time. Coming back too early resets the wait; gone long enough, the exchange is done when you come back.
help.trade.delay_hours.tip: Coming back too early starts the wait again.
help.trade.margin.what: What the trader keeps for herself on each swap. The player never sees it.
help.trade.margin.tip: "Exact value": the lowest and highest share, in percent.
help.trade.item.what: What the trader brings: the item, then how many.
help.trade.item.game: The amount is drawn on each visit. A trader only sells items that have a price in the trade, so the item list of the stock only offers those.
help.trade.item.tip: "Add what she sells" opens the list: search, tick, add.
help.trade.accept.what: What the voice takes as payment: whole categories, single items, or both.
help.trade.accept.game: The player can only pay with these items. A list only counts what traders buy.
help.trade.accept.tip: At least one list or item. Hover a list to see its items.
help.trade.group.what: A bundle: items that share one total.
help.trade.group.game: At each visit, the game draws the total, then shares it among the bundle's items.
help.trade.group.example: Seeds: between 3 and 8 items in all, no more than 4 different items
help.trade.group.tip: Add the items from the bundle's card. The game refuses an empty bundle.
help.note.item.what: The item that carries the note, picked in the list of the game's items.
help.note.item.tip: A new voice writes its text instead.
help.note.key.what: The base name of the texts of the note.
help.note.key.game: The player reads these texts by inspecting the note.
help.note.key.tip: A new voice writes its text instead.
help.note.loot.what: Themed furniture on top of the papers, and whether it is rare or common there.
help.note.loot.game: The player finds it while searching, then reads the frequency.
help.note.loot.tip: Optional: the note is already wherever papers are found.
help.note.glovebox.what: Glove boxes of special vehicles on top of the ordinary cars.
help.note.glovebox.tip: Optional: the note is already in ordinary glove boxes.
help.note.text.what: What is written on the note, one line at a time. The button puts in her frequency.
help.note.text.game: The player finds the note in the loot and reads this text by inspecting it.
help.note.text.tip: 8 lines of 40 signs at most, no < > ^; one line gives her frequency.
newtype.talker.help: Tells stories, gives advice, keeps you company.
newtype.missions.help: Asks for help and gives rewards.
scale.head.call_one_in.rare.help: About one call every 12 game hours.
scale.head.call_one_in.sometimes.help: About one call every 6 game hours.
scale.head.call_one_in.often.help: About one call every 3 game hours.
scale.trade.delay_hours.now.help: She comes as soon as you leave.
scale.trade.margin.generous.help: She keeps little for herself: good deals.
scale.trade.margin.greedy.help: She keeps a lot: her prices are hard.
checkname.name: the name
checkname.label: the name
marks.question: Which places can she mark on the map?
marks.help: Tick the markers she gives to players.
